name: calendars_list
description: List every calendar of every connected Outlook.com, Microsoft 365 and Google account, each naming its account and provider, its calendarId, whether it is that account's default, whether the account owns it - one merely shared with it is not owned - and its owner's address, its access - edit, read, or freeBusy where Google lets only busy time be read - hidden where the person hid it from their Google list, its own time zone where Google keeps one - Outlook keeps none per calendar - and, under busyShownIn, each other account its busy time shows in. An account that could not be read, or whose events the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why, and one holding more calendars than one answer carries under cutShort.

name: events_list
description: Read the events of a period across every connected calendar, earliest first, or latest first with newestFirst. query finds the events whose title, description, place, organizer or guests hold every word it names - a person by name or address included - on every account: Google searches its own, while Outlook, which searches titles alone, is read across the period and matched here. account, with provider where two share an address, reads that account alone, and calendarId, as calendars_list names it, that one of its calendars alone. Each event answers once, naming under copies every account and calendar holding it, with that copy's id, how it shows there and that account's own answer. An occurrence of a recurring series names under originalStart the start its series gave it, which a moved one keeps, and under each copy that account's seriesId. A calendar shared into one account from another connected account is read through its owner alone. Lumman's own busy copies - private blocks titled "Busy · <the address of the account it copies> (Multi Calendar connector)" - are never among the events: busyCopies answers them apart, one entry per copied busy time with its start and end, the account it copies under copyOf - unknown where no record of it stands - and each account it stands in under standsIn. None counts as the person's time or can be moved or cancelled; asked about one, say it is a busy copy of that account, switched off at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar or by taking that pair away with busy_everywhere_set. Every time is given with its offset in the zone the answer names under timeZone: the one passed, else the person's stored zone, which now names with their time now; an all-day event's start and end are dates, its end the day after its last. An answer, a guest's or an account's own, is accepted, tentative, declined, unanswered or organizer, and one a copy cannot know is left out. An event names its kind where it is no ordinary event - a Google outOfOffice, focusTime, workingLocation, birthday or fromGmail entry - its privacy where it is not normal: public, private, confidential or personal - and its Teams, Zoom or Meet join link, and each copy its webLink; an out-of-office event shows as away. A description is its first 255 characters, marked descriptionCut where it goes on: events_get reads it. Where more events are read than one answer carries, the last in its order are left out and counted under leftOut with the period holding them all: read that period again, narrower or one calendar at a time. A meeting whose guests alone one answer cannot carry names the first that fit, omittedAttendees counting the rest. Each calendar answers at most 50 events, read in time order; one with more is named under cutShort with its calendarId, readTo - the start of the last event read - and continueAt: pass that continueAt with its account and calendarId, the same period and query, to read on from exactly where it stopped; read latest first, such a calendar's latest events are the ones past readTo, so read it on before naming the latest. A calendar or an account that could not be read, or that the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why: needs_reconnection - reconnected at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar - not_allowed, refused, gone, rate_limited or unavailable; where nothing could be read the answer is an error. malformed counts events a provider sent in a form that could not be read, each left out. An event whose words screen as a prompt attack is left out and named under withheld by its start, its end and each copy's account, calendarId and id - by account alone where an id screened so - and a calendar whose name screened so is named by its account alone.

name: events_get
description: Read one event whole, by the account, calendarId and id events_list names: its description as text - cut where one answer cannot carry it all, omittedCharacters counting what was left out, which reads at its web link - every Teams, Zoom or Meet join link found in the event, its place or its words, the organizer and each guest with their role - required, optional or resource - and answer, the first that fit where one answer cannot carry them all, omittedAttendees counting the rest; its kind and privacy as events_list names them, how it shows, the account's own answer, its reminders - the minutes before its start each sounds, or none, which events_edit writes as an empty list, and unsaid where a Google event keeps its calendar's own - and its web link. Times are given as events_list gives them, in the zone named under timeZone, and an occurrence of a recurring series its seriesId and originalStart as events_list names them. An event whose words screen as a prompt attack is withheld. One of Lumman's own busy copies is answered under busyCopy as events_list answers one, saying under about what it is and where it is switched off.

name: free_times_find
description: Find when the person is free in every connected calendar: each stretch of a window that no busy time touches and that is at least as long as the meeting. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none. An all-day event holding time holds its whole day in the person's own time zone. The search never starts before now, keeps to every preference preferences_get names and to the window's first 365 days and, where the call names them, to hours on each day and to weekdays on top of those preferences; limit keeps the earliest stretches. Once any day has working hours, a day without them is off. The buffers pad the meeting being booked: a stretch starts buffer_before_minutes after busy time ends and ends buffer_after_minutes before the next begins. Each stretch answers once, in time order, with its parts inside the preferred times under preferred. Times, hours and weekdays are in the zone the call names, else the person's own; the stored working hours and preferred times are in the person's own. searched names the window searched and narrowedBy what narrowed it: notice, the least notice from now, rounded up to the quarter hour; horizon, to the end of its last day; yearCap, the 365 days; readLimit, a calendar holding more events than a search reads, read as far as it could be and searched to two days before the last it read; daysOff, days without working hours; fullDays, days already holding the most meetings in a day, a meeting being an event of some length that holds time inside that day's working hours. A calendar or account named under unread was not counted, nor were the calendars past the first 100 of an account under cutShort, so their busy time may fall inside a stretch; an account needing reconnection is reconnected at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar.

name: events_create
description: Create an event in one of a connected account's own calendars: the one named by the calendarId calendars_list gives, else the account's default; a calendar only shared with the account is refused. Guests are invited by that account's provider, Microsoft or Google, from its own address. A timed event's start and end are instants with their offset, the end no earlier than the start, so an entry of no length is taken; an all-day event's are dates, its end the day after its last. It is written in the person's own time zone, so an invitation shows that zone's time, and the answer gives its times in the zone it names under timeZone. A meeting with guests, no location and no video gets the person's default meeting link as its place. How it shows, its privacy, reminders, kind and video link are each refused with the reason where the account's provider lacks them. An Outlook subject takes at most 255 characters. repeat makes it a recurring series, each occurrence keeping the start's own hour in the person's time zone across clock changes. Who hears of it is notify's choice. Repeating a create whose answer was lost, with the same arguments, finds the event the first made rather than making a second - for the rest of that day (UTC), on Outlook only while Microsoft also recognises the repeat - so two events meant as two differ in some argument. Each guest's own times are answered under guestTimes in their time zone where it is known - the one guestZones names for them, else the one a member of the person's circles stored - and any other guest's zone as unknown, their time counted as the person's. A meeting any part of which falls, for a guest of known zone, outside 09:00-18:00 or on a Saturday or Sunday in that zone - an all-day one only on a Saturday or Sunday - is not sent: the refusal names each such guest and their time, and it goes out only once the call passes unusualHoursAgreed true on the person's word. A series is checked by its first occurrence; the person's own hours are never held.

name: events_edit
description: Change an event the account organises, in place and in one call: its subject, body, location, start and end, how it shows, its privacy, reminders and video link, and its guests - addGuests invited, removeGuests taken off. Only what is named changes: the event keeps its id, every other guest's answer and its join link, a start named alone keeps its length and an end named alone keeps its start. Start and end are named as events_create names them, so naming both in the other form turns a timed event all-day or back, and are written in the person's own time zone as events_create writes them. What the account's provider lacks is refused with the reason, as on events_create, and so is a new body for an Outlook online meeting, whose join details it holds. Changing guests takes inviting allowed on the account. A whole series' start and end are its first occurrence's, and a change to a whole series holding occurrences changed apart from it is refused, naming each by when its series set it, so none of theirs is undone. Its provider sends a meeting's guests the change from the account's own address, as notify chooses. Like every write, the answer names the event's provider, its calendarId where its provider addresses it by one, and its webLink. Guests' own hours hold a change as they hold events_create: every guest's where its times change, an added guest's at its time otherwise.

name: events_cancel
description: Cancel an event the account organises; its provider sends a meeting's attendees the cancellation from that account's own address, as notify chooses, and Outlook sends message with it. Someone else's event is not cancelled here: declining it with events_respond takes it off an Outlook calendar and leaves it on a Google one, shown declined. copyOnly true takes only the account's own copy of someone else's event off its calendar - an Outlook copy its organiser has cancelled included - sending nothing, though Google then shows the account as declined and so needs inviting and replying allowed.

name: events_respond
description: Accept, tentatively accept or decline an invitation; the account's provider sends the answer, with message where given, to its organiser from the account's own address unless notify is none. Answering a whole series answers each occurrence answered apart from it too, and says under replaced how many of their answers it replaced.

name: preferences_get
description: Read the person's scheduling preferences, as preferences_set describes each, null where unset; once any day's hours are set, a day without is off; receiving names the calendar bookings are made in. calendars_list says which calendars count as busy.

name: preferences_set
description: Change any of the person's scheduling preferences as preferences_get names them, the rest left as they stand; null clears one. calendar marks one calendar calendars_list names as counting as busy or not. receiving, which null does not clear, names the calendar bookings are made in: one of an account's own calendars, as calendars_list names it. time_zone changes only with zoneConfirmed true, once the person has confirmed it as theirs.

name: busy_everywhere_set
description: Show one of an account's own calendars as busy in another connected account the person names, or stop: within minutes each busy event of the coming 60 days appears as a private block titled "Busy · <the calendar's account address> (Multi Calendar connector)" in the main calendar of the account named, while it allows changing events - never in another calendar, and never in an account nobody named, one connected later included - one block per busy time however many calendars named into it hold it. A block moves with its event, goes when the event ends or goes or the pair is taken away, and is placed again if removed by hand; events_list answers blocks apart from events under busyCopies, and no tool counts, moves or cancels one. Naming a pair answers under shows the sentence to give the person word for word. calendars_list names each calendarId and the accounts each calendar already shows busy in.

name: booking_links_create
description: Make a link offering times free_times_find found for a named meeting, for the person to send to one guest. The guest, with no account, picks one of these times in their own time zone and gives a name and address; the time is checked again against every calendar and the person's working hours, buffers, notice and daily maximum, and booked once, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings; a time no longer free is replaced by others up to the link's last, within those hours - Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00 where they stored none. The answer names the link's id and when it closes, 14 days after it is made, and a time after then is refused. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so put the person's own name in subject, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

name: booking_page_set
description: Set one of the person's permanent booking pages, named by the name it answers at on this site: the one they hold by that name changes in the fields given alone, newName moving it to a new address while its old one answers nothing; a name they hold no page by adds a page, which needs subject and stays until the account goes. Anyone opening a page, with no account, sees up to 20 times free in every calendar within the person's working hours - Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00 where they stored none - and every other preference, spread across the coming 14 days, each day's preferred times first, in their own time zone, and books one by giving a name and address, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings; a time is booked once across all their pages. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so put the person's own name in subject, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

name: polls_create
description: Make a poll of times free_times_find found for a named meeting, for the people it is for. Each address gets its own link, an address named twice one, handed back in this answer alone - a lost link needs a new poll. Lumman sends them nothing: hand the links to the person to share, or send each from the person's own mailbox. Whoever opens a link, with no account, ticks the times that address can make, answering again replaces its answer, and sees no one else's. polls_results ranks the times and polls_book books one, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings, which making a poll does not need; a poll closes once booked, or 14 days after it is made, and then holds no address or answer. Naming a circle makes a poll for members of it or, on the person's own circle, for addresses invited that have not joined, meant for those circles_free_times_find names under noCalendar or notJoined: once they answer, the person's own searches for that circle count each by the times they can make, and their page offers to connect a calendar - an address that has not joined joins first, through the link circles_invite gave it. A member with a calendar is read through it, never from a poll. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so put the person's own name in subject, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An invitee whose time zone is known, as events_create knows a guest's, is answered with that zone and each time in it.

name: polls_results
description: Read a poll's answers: each of its times still to come with the addresses of those who can make it, most first, then each address it is for and whether it has answered. An answer is what that address's own link sent. A booked or closed poll holds none; booked names the time it was booked, or is being booked, at.

name: polls_book
description: Book one of a poll's times in the calendar the person named to receive bookings: the time is checked again against every calendar, exactly the people the poll is for are invited by Microsoft or Google from that account's own address, the meeting written in the person's own time zone, and the poll closes. Its invitees' own hours hold it as they hold events_create, save for one who ticked that time, chosen on their own clock. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

name: links_polls_list
description: List the person's booking links and group polls still open or being booked, oldest first - each link with its id, meeting, state, when it closes and the times it still offers, each poll with its id, meeting, state, who it is for, how many have answered and the times someone can make, most first - every booking page with its address, and every booking a link, poll or page took for a time 30 days ago or later, never who booked it. One being booked for longer than a booking takes is stuck, and links_polls_close closes it. polls_results reads a poll's answers.

name: links_polls_close
description: Close one of the person's booking links or group polls still open or being booked: its page answers closed from then on, and a poll's addresses and answers are deleted. A meeting the provider made for one being booked stays: events_list shows whether it was. links_polls_list names each.

name: circles_invite
description: Invite people by address into one of the person's own circles: an existing one by its id, as circles_list names it, or one by its name, matched whatever its case and made where the person has none by it - two of the person's circles whose names differ only in case are refused, naming both ids. The answer names the circle's id and whether it was made. Each address newly invited gets its own link, which only an account signed in at that address can join with; an address already invited keeps the link it was sent and is named under kept, unless reissue asks for a new one, which stops the old. Lumman sends invitees nothing: hand the links to the person to share, or send each from the person's own mailbox.

name: circles_list
description: List every circle the person owns or has joined: its id, its name, whether it is the person's own, the address of each member who has joined and, on the person's own, of each address invited that has not joined under invited. circles_free_times_find finds a time for one.

name: circles_free_times_find
description: Find when everyone in one of the person's circles is free: each stretch of a window that no member's busy time touches and that is at least as long as the meeting, in the zone the call names, else the person's own - the same whichever member asks, save for a member with no calendar connected, counted by the asker's own polls. The calendars each member owns and counts as busy - never one someone else shared with them - are read through that member's own connection as the call is made, and come back under busy only as when that member is busy - the circle's owner named owner, every other member by the address invited - never what an event says. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none. An all-day event holding time holds its whole day in its member's time zone; no one's stored working hours or other preferences apply, only the hours and weekdays the call names, in the answer's zone; limit keeps the earliest stretches, and the search keeps to the window's first 365 days. A member none of whose calendars could be read is named under unknown, and one only some of whose could under readInPart, their busy time read counted; either's busy time may fall inside a stretch. A member with no calendar connected counts as free only at the times they ticked in the person's own polls for this circle, and until they answer one is named under noCalendar - polls_create naming the circle asks them. On the person's own circle each address invited that has not joined is named under notJoined and counts the same way once it answers such a poll. Anyone counted by polls whose answers tick no time in the window is named under tickedNothing. Each stretch names under members every other member's own time for it in the zone they stored, marked unusual where any of it falls outside 09:00-18:00 or on a Saturday or Sunday there. circles_list names each circle's id.
